quote_text:
Can you just talk us through that  from your side of perspective for... 
Um, look, we always knew it was  going to be a difficult task,  
you know, given what was on the line for Celtic. 
You know, we've probably been a little  bit unfortunate with the way that the  
fixtures have fell — could have done with  this one maybe two or three weeks' time  
when the league was all wrapped up. But, you know, it sounds bizarre to  
sit here and say, for the opening half  an hour I thought we were very good. 
I thought, you know, the shape of the team  was good and we got aggressive with the press,  
forced Celtic into playing a lot longer  than they would normally have liked.
But, um, you know, the first goal  was a real kick in the teeth given,  
you know, it's an own goal,  it's a bit of misfortune. 
And then the second one, you know, comes  from a promising attack that we had,  
you know — a tame effort on goal — but then  within five or six seconds, with the pace  
of Celtic on the counter-attack, the  ball ends up in the back of your net. 
And then, um, yeah, we've got a  mountain to climb from that point on.
I know, I know it's strange — game finishes  five — but that opening 30 minutes, do you  
feel that was some of the best you've played  both with and without the ball against them? 
Yeah, arguably it was. I mean, it was a different approach  
to what we've done, you know, in the past. You know, you're kind of damned if you do  
and damned if you don't sometimes, you know. You can sit off the game and sit in a low block  
for 90 minutes and try and contain them and hope  to hit them on the break — or you can do what we  
tried to do, which was to go and get after them  at the top end of the pitch and force turnovers. 
And I thought in that opening 30  minutes we done that numerous times. 
We got lots of crosses into the box. But, um, you know, Celtic with the  
quality that they have — you know, Brendan  Rodgers' tactical nous — they soon figure  
you out and they find a way to break you down. And, you know, I don't think it'll be a great  
surprise to most people out there, you  know, that Celtic have won here today. 
But obviously we're a bit embarrassed  ourselves with the way the scoreline looks.
Yeah, I mean, look — obviously the players,  you know, we've all got personal pride,  
and nobody likes to be on the  end of a scoreline like that. 
But, you know, look, I take  responsibility as the manager. 
I've, you know, asked the players  to go and play a certain way. 
You know, the timings of the goal — you  could argue at 2-0 down could we have  
managed the game a little bit better and got  to half-time with the scoreline being two? 
They score three or four minutes into added-on  time in the first half, and then they score two  
minutes right after the break. And at that point then for us  
it's about damage limitations, you know. We take off the likes of Dalby and Docherty  
just to try and, um, protect them a little bit  — we can't afford any injuries to those two.
And, um, look, I'm not going to  be overly critical of the players. 
We're disappointed, of course we are. But, you know, that group have  
put us in a really good position. They've fought extremely hard all season  
to make sure we got the top six, and we're still  very much in the fight for, you know, third place. 
We'll wait and see what happens  at Pittodrie this afternoon. 
But we can't dwell on this one. We have to pick ourselves up,  
and we have to make sure we're ready  for another difficult fixture next.
Can't detract from what's been a good  season because you still are — it could  
be a cracking end to your season next matches. 
Yeah, I mean, look — we don't want  the season to peter out, you know. 
And, um, you know, we're not  satisfied with just finishing fifth. 
You know, we really want to try and keep  the pressure on Aberdeen and Hibs above us. 
But, you know, that's what happens in the top half  of the table — you end up playing the best teams  
in the league and those fixtures are always a  lot harder than the ones in the bottom half.
But this is the position that we want to be in. 
This is the position that we  fought hard to put ourselves in. 
And, um, you know, we'll keep  fighting right till the end. 
I don't think today was a case of, you know, lack  of effort or commitment on the players' part. 
You know, we came up against  the best team in the country. 
And when Celtic play the way they did for  the last hour, with the speed in the game,  
they can do that to any team. You know, I think that's three games  
in a row now where they've scored five goals. So, you know, credit to them, congratulations  
to Brendan Rodgers and to his players  — and they thoroughly deserve to enjoy  
the celebrations tonight because they have by a  country mile been the best team in the country.
How much confidence do you have in your side that  they can finish better than fifth this season? 
Well, look, I mean, I've said it numerous  times — you get greedy, don't you? 
You know, I mean, start of the  season we all would have probably,  
you know, accepted finishing seventh or eighth. 
The fact that we've finished in the top  half I think is a great achievement. 
But now everybody's talking about Europe. So the pressure is still on, very much so. 
And, um, you know, we want to experience  European football as well as a staff  
and as a group of players — because a  lot of us have never had that before. 
So still a hell of a lot to play for. We're obviously, you know,  
apologetic to the supporters today for  the way that the game just petered out.
You know, they've been really significant all  season in the support that they've gave the team. 
And, you know, we're going to need  them over the next four games. 
And, um, you know, we'll not allow this  one to affect the psychology of the group. 
We'll pick ourselves up and we'll go again.
Stopped by a kind of fairly unusual protest  — was that a hindrance, was it frustrating? 
Um, yeah, I mean, look —  it's not ideal, obviously. 
I mean at that particular moment in  time, I think it was around 25 minutes,  
I felt that we were — you know — we  were really competitive at that stage. 
And, you know, we certainly  didn't want a break in play. 
But yeah, look, these things happen. It was a bit of a strange situation — not  
one that I've experienced before. Um, but yeah.
title: ‘I apologise to the fans’ Jim Goodwin Post Match Interview | Dundee United 0-5 Celtic
